what: Sixteen kernels from a DeepSeek-R1-Qwen-Distilled decode step: eleven decode kernels and five teaching primitives. The baseline the Rust frontend is developed against.

representations.tile-rs: Rust source against the tile intrinsics, HAND-WRITTEN -- not one of these sixteen files carries the lift's `Generated by ptoas_rs` header, and that is the point: this column is what a person would write, where the `tile` column is what the emitters receive. COMPILED: all 16 build against the kernel-side DSL on the pinned nightly, checked by crates/ptoas_rs/tests/bench_tile_rs_compiles.rs. This note previously read 'CORPUS ONLY -- it is not compiled here ... Do not read these as verified', which was true until the DSL was carried into this tree.
representations.tile: tile-dialect MLIR, in the llvm.func + hacc.entry + __tile_* form the emitters consume. This is a CAPTURE: it is the truth about what the emitters receive, and silent about what a person would write.
representations.pto: PTO assembly, regenerated from the .tile by the in-tree rspto. Every file here is reproducible, and a test asserts it byte for byte.
representations.ascendc: AscendC C++ for bisheng, regenerated from the .tile by the in-tree pto-to-ascendc. Reproducible, and a test asserts it byte for byte. Emission is for a named part (--soc, default 910b): a blank target has no unified buffer, so every kernel would appear to overflow.

refusal_is_a_result: Two kernels have no .pto and no .cpp, and that is correct rather than missing data. Both exceed a hardware bound, and each records why -- separately per representation, because the two emitters check different bounds and happen to agree here. The reshaped variants under fixed/ are the same computations at widths that fit.

reshaped.why: NOT a resource reshape, despite what this field said until 2026-11-02 -- that text was copied from `argmax`, whose capture really is refused for unified-buffer size. This capture calls `__tile_attention_gqa_f32(dst, q, k, v, heads_q, heads_kv, seq_len, head_dim)` with its operands SHIFTED BY ONE and an extra `causal` the surviving declaration does not carry, so `v` receives a constant. The AscendC emitter refuses it on exactly that ground; the PTO emitter accepts it and emits attention over the wrong operands. This variant is the same computation with the operands in the declared order.
reshaped.pto_does_not_assemble: and the corrected call then reaches a defect of OUR OWN that the shifted one never could: the gqa arm reuses the whole-operand partition view's SSA for the per-head slice, so `%pto3` is defined `!pto.partition_tensor_view<32x64xf32>` and used as `<16x64xf32>`, and ptoas rejects the module. Reachable only when heads_q and heads_kv give Q and K/V different row counts -- the GQA case.

reshaped.why: the captured shape is refused for hardware-resource reasons; this is the same computation at a tile width that fits.

gate_up_silu.chunk_note: placed by the chunked path at 4480 (two chunks of 8960). The fused arm used to build its output type from the CALL's extents while the tiles were chunk-sized, producing `ins(...4480...) outs(...8960...)` that ptoas accepted; it now trusts the tiles when chunking.

argmax.pto_refused: NPU tile bound (arch a2a3): the row-major data tile spans multiple 512B fractals with a bad stride.

reshaped.why: the captured shape is refused for hardware-resource reasons; this is the same computation at a tile width that fits.

argmax.ascendc_refused: UB overflow: buffer 0 needs 607744 bytes, larger than the whole unified buffer.

reshaped.why: the capture passes 5 operands where `__tile_matmul_f16` declares 6, omitting `dst`. The PTO emitter carries a second contract at 5 operands and silently reinterpreted it, parsing m=64 for a kernel whose A operand is 1x64; the result was correct anyway because the accumulator's shape comes from the A tile. The cost was two dead full-operand UB tiles and their DMA loads, which the corrected call removes -- 4 fewer operations, identical tmatmul and tstore.

estimated_decode_kernels.source: the playground baseline set, defined as sixteen kernels, and the published registry's paper collection names the same sixteen
estimated_decode_kernels.what_it_is: The number of distinct kernels one decode step of this model needs -- the denominator the representation counts are read against. Where the count is KNOWN it is used; where it is not, inventory() derives a LOWER BOUND from the model's own configuration. Not a measurement of a running engine in either case.
estimated_decode_kernels.derivation_error: the inventory predicted 15 for DeepSeek V4 Flash against a registry count of 52, so it under-counts by about 3.5x. Not applied as a correction: one anchor cannot calibrate a model, and a derivation multiplied by 3.5 would look measured and would not be.
estimated_decode_kernels.a_kernel_is: one distinct (operation, shape) pair, because that is what this corpus holds -- one rmsnorm file serves every block that shares D. A layer count does not multiply it.

inventory.line: rmsnorm at D (attn_norm, ffn_norm and the final norm share it)
attention projections: q, k, v, output
dense FFN gate/up at DENSE_FFN_INTER, and down at D

estimated_decode_kernels.inventory_is_not_used_here: the inventory derives 13 and the known count is 16. The known count wins; the inventory is kept because the gap between them is the measurement of how coarse it is.

what_the_inventory_collapses.each expert's gate, up and down are one: a real engine has three kernels there, and the gate/up pair is often fused separately from the down-projection
what_the_inventory_collapses.one attention core: decode, prefill and partial/chunked are different kernels with different shapes, and a model with two attention types doubles that again
what_the_inventory_collapses.one matvec per projection: f16 and f32 weight forms are separate kernels, and each quantisation the engine supports adds another (q8_0, q4_K, iq2_xxs, mxfp4 ...)
what_the_inventory_collapses.no prefill shapes: every projection and norm has a batched prefill form, which is a different kernel from its decode form
what_the_inventory_collapses.no quantise/dequantise kernels: activation quantisation and weight unpacking are real kernels; the inventory treats weight format as out of scope
what_the_inventory_collapses.one sampling kernel: argmax is counted; top-p, top-k sampling and draft verification are not

estimated_decode_kernels.why_collapses_are_listed_not_multiplied: 'under-counts by 3.5x' is one number and tells a reader nothing they can act on. These name the specific rows that each stand for several real kernels. They are not multiplied out: that would turn a list of known omissions into a fabricated total. Someone who knows the true count for this model can see which rows to expand.
estimated_decode_kernels.published_registry: the published kernel registry, read 2026-11-02, carries the sixteen-kernel paper collection this corpus was built from, and the two hold the same sixteen names with no extras on either side. The corpus was assembled from a different tree two months after the registry was generated, so the agreement is independent corroboration of the one denominator here that is a definition rather than an estimate.

stored_pto_that_does_not_assemble.pto/fixed/attn_gqa.pto: the stored .pto does NOT assemble: the gqa arm reuses the whole-operand partition view's SSA for the per-head slice, so `%pto3` is defined `!pto.partition_tensor_view<32x64xf32>` and used as `<16x64xf32>`. One value with two types is invalid in any MLIR. Reachable only when heads_q and heads_kv give Q and K/V different row counts -- the GQA case -- so the arm is broken for exactly the shape it exists to serve.
stored_pto_that_does_not_assemble.how_this_went_unnoticed: the corpus had a byte-identity gate over its PTO and it was green. That gate re-runs the emitter and compares against the stored file, so an invalid emission matches an invalid artefact: reproducibility is not validity. A second gate now assembles every stored .pto (rust/crates/pto_to_ascendc/tests/stored_pto_assembles.rs).
